_comment: Cursor-pagination coverage over the LIVE OpenAPI corpus (ADR-0150). Until governance/check/cursor-pagination-coverage/tests/cursor_pagination_coverage.rs landed, this doctrine had never produced a verdict about this codebase: the kernel's only consumer was marketplace/facade/dev-cli, which no workflow invokes, so every case it had ever run was one of the four hand-written fixtures inside src/lib.rs. Both frozen lists are SETS of keys pinned by EQUALITY and therefore TWO-SIDED: a new finding blocks (ADR-0150 is mandatory, so a new collection endpoint without cursor pagination is born-blocking), and a repaired one ALSO blocks until it is struck from the list in the same change. One-sided ceilings cannot tell debt-paid-off from a scan that collapsed. Keys are route-anchored, never line-anchored, so an edit above an operation does not force a blind re-freeze. The min_* floors are the anti-vacuity oracle; every one counts SUBJECTS (documents, operations, capabilities, tracked paths) and never findings, so declaring cursor + page_size on an endpoint moves the frozen set and leaves every floor exactly where it is.
subject: tracked *.yaml / *.yml whose first-column `openapi:` marks them an OpenAPI description — the same corpus boundary the sibling idempotency-key-coverage gate uses, so the two agree about what the contract corpus IS
_measured_2026_08_19: Measured on dev @ bc6e04fa1: 138 OpenAPI documents across 68 capabilities over 13761 tracked paths, 469 `get:` operations of which 60 are collection-shaped. All 60 collection-shaped gets lack the cursor + page_size pair — the covered count is ZERO, so this doctrine has never once been satisfied by this repository. Exactly one forbidden offset/page parameter exists. Two of the 138 documents (console/contracts/openapi-v1.yaml, gateway/connector/contracts/openapi-v1.yaml) are invisible to `git grep -E '^openapi:'` because git classifies them as binary; the walk decodes lossily and reads them anyway, which is why the census says 138 and a grep says 136.
_frozen_offset_or_page_comment: ADR-0150 FORBIDS offset/page pagination, and every Oyatie-authored contract in this tree obeys: the single frozen key is a captured snapshot of a THIRD-PARTY API (Workday REST v40, servers: https://wd2-impl-services1.workday.com), where the offset parameter is a fact about Workday's API that no change here can repair. It is frozen rather than excluded on purpose: dropping vendor snapshots from the corpus would narrow the scan to make the number pretty, and the other nine connector snapshots are read on exactly the same terms. Pinned by EQUALITY over the whole set, never by a floor — a floor on a term whose honest target is zero goes red the moment the corpus is clean, and a guard that reds on success gets deleted.
